items.text: WTI and Brent both down ~4% on the week (to $83.9 and $88.2), easing from geopolitical shock but still elevated on Middle East tensions. Energy credit spreads tightening modestly; watch for commodity-linked corporate refinancing risk if prices sustain.

July payrolls crashed -23K vs +20K prior, shocking after months of resilience. Unemployment ticked to 4.1%; claims at 203K show no panic yet. Fed data-dependent risk rising—this is the kind of miss that can trigger pivot signals and distressed hiring sector defaults.

Core PCE at 2.47% YoY (July), down from 2.57%; headline CPI 3.3%, down from 3.46%. Core stuck above 2%, long-term expectations at 3.3% per Michigan survey. Sticky core leaves room for more cuts, but 1-yr inflation expectations rising to 4.3% (up from 4.2%)—wage-price-service spiral risk live.

ECB deposit rate unchanged at 2.25%; fed funds at 3.75%. UST curve at 47 bps, flattening from 50 bps, as long end pressured by growth rebound fears and sticky inflation. Credit spreads face two-way risk: labor shock could drive cuts/spreads tighter, but sticky core may cap relief.

HY OAS at 267 bps (down 3 from 270), IG at 80 (down 1). CCC-rated credit at 1031 bps, modestly cheaper. Payroll shock hasn't spurred credit widening—market still pricing soft landing. Watch for widening if August labor data repeats.

ISM Manufacturing PMI rose to 55.6 in July, marking seventh consecutive month of expansion and strongest reading since May 2022. GDPNow at 4.61% (vs 1.54% prior month), buoyed by July strength, but services employment contracting and consumer sentiment collapsing suggest front-loading. Q3 growth likely front-loaded.

University of Michigan consumer sentiment fell to 51 in early August 2026, down from 55.2 in July and below market expectations of 54.5, ending two consecutive months of improvement. Housing starts down 125 bps YoY to 1.239M; existing home sales sliding. Mortgage rates at 6.66%, offsetting sentiment deterioration.

themeCards.title: Payroll Cliff & Labor Shock
themeCards.statusLine: Unexpected July nonfarm payroll decline of 23,000 jobs and unemployment holding at 4.1% has shattered 'resilient labor' narrative. August data risk is very live.
themeCards.relevance: First negative print in 4+ years raises recession whispers and Fed cut acceleration risk. Distressed sectors (retail, logistics, hospitality) may face covenant stress; BBB/HY refinancers dependent on equity rally face mark-to-market risk if spreads widen on growth shock.

themeCards.title: Consumer Sentiment Cliff
themeCards.statusLine: Deterioration was broad-based across political and demographic groups, with particularly sharp declines among older, lower-income and less-educated consumers. Expectations for business conditions also worsened significantly, falling 11% over next year and 17% over longer term.
themeCards.relevance: Michigan sentiment down 8% MoM to 51 (lowest since mid-year panic). Consumer discretionary, retail, restaurant, travel credits under pressure if savings rate squeeze continues. Wage-less consumers (30%+ of lower quintile) face debt stress risk into 4Q.

themeCards.title: China Demand Contraction
themeCards.statusLine: NBS Manufacturing PMI declined to 49.2 in July from 50.3 in June, also missing market expectations and indicating a contraction in factory activity. Output, new orders, and export orders all fell.
themeCards.relevance: Weak China demand ripples to US capital goods, electronics, auto supply, and apparel manufacturers. Cyclical credit (industrials, autos) faces earnings downside; refinancing windows for China-exposed issuers may narrow if sentiment stays soft.

themeCards.title: Energy Price Volatility & Geopolitical Risk
themeCards.statusLine: WTI/Brent down 4% WoW but well above Feb 2026 lows; Iran tensions remain acute. Oil volatility (VIX 15.2) suggests complacency. One supply shock re-escalates energy credits and EM currency stress.
themeCards.relevance: Upstream/downstream refiners, shipping, and small-cap E&P names face mark-to-market risk on hedges. Distressed energy credits (sub-investment) have very thin margins if oil bounces above $95; structured credit tied to commodity collateral exposed.

themeCards.title: Sticky Core PCE & Wage Expectations
themeCards.statusLine: Core PCE 2.47%, down but sticky above 2%. Michigan 1-yr inflation expectations jumped to 4.3%; only 8% of consumers expect income growth to beat inflation. Wage growth (3.15%) decelerating but residual service inflation elevated.
themeCards.relevance: Fed may not have room to cut aggressively despite payroll shock. Floating-rate credit, refinancers, and service-heavy credit (healthcare, hospitality) face margin compression if rates stay high. Covenant resets and interest coverage ratios tighten if rates don't fall faster than consensus.

themeCards.title: Manufacturing Strength vs. Services Employment Divergence
themeCards.statusLine: ISM Manufacturing PMI rose to 55.6 in July, marking seventh consecutive month of expansion and strongest reading since May 2022. Yet July services employment contracted and July services prices remain sticky at 70.3.
themeCards.relevance: Goods export/AI-driven capex boom masking underlying service-sector labor softness. Implies front-loaded Q3 growth, payroll risk in Q4. Credit investors face divergent spreads: cyclical manufacturers may re-rate tighter on demand strength, but labor-intensive services (hospitality, logistics) face downside as hiring slows. Widening basis risk between sectors.

regime.label: Mid-Cycle Inflection
regime.detail: Manufacturing surge masking labor cliff; core sticky above 2%, sentiment cratering; spreads tight despite downside risks; refinancing window narrowing.
